item.text: {"text":"The official SASRec implementation scores candidates by dot product between the final sequence representation and candidate embeddings drawn from the same item table used for sequence inputs. Its `predict(sess, u, seq, item_idx)` returns raw logits; sigmoid is applied in the training loss, not prediction. The original TensorFlow implementation hardcodes 101 candidate IDs, so its interface requires adaptation for other candidate counts or full-catalog scoring. No auxiliary transition-graph scoring branch appears in this model. [Official model source](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py)\n\nImplementation inference: a residual transition score could be combined with SASRec logits as `score = sasrec_logit + alpha * transition_score(history, candidate)`, provided the scoring hook receives history or features that explicitly retain the branch’s required information. The supplied `predict_score(features, items)` contract alone does not establish that access. A positive global temperature or candidate-independent offset preserves ranking and therefore cannot improve HR@10 by itself; a candidate-dependent residual can change rankings. An inference ablation setting `alpha=0` would measure the branch’s contribution for the same checkpoint, while separately training a baseline would test its training-time effect. Public source establishes the reference architecture only; local model code, checkpoint contents, and predictor writer must establish whether a branch actually exists and is restored during inference."}
